focus: Overlap load and compute with ping-pong buffers or a canonical dataflow schedule.
merge_rule: Union of gemm_flatten_v1 and flash_no_RMW overlay. On id conflicts, the no-RMW overlay replaces the v1 entry.

skills.pattern: #pragma HLS DATAFLOW placed inside a tile loop using non-unit increment such as for (tile_i = 0; tile_i < N; tile_i += TILE_SIZE)
skills.strategy: Do not place DATAFLOW inside tile_i += TILE_SIZE loops. Use a unit-increment tile index and compute the base offset outside the dataflow region.
required_steps: detect DATAFLOW pragma nested under tile_i += TILE_SIZE or similar non-unit outer loop
replace with for (int tile = 0; tile < NUM_TILES; tile++) and tile_i = tile * TILE_SIZE
move #pragma HLS DATAFLOW to a helper called once per tile with canonical load/compute/store calls
keep dynamic tail handling inside subfunctions, not as control flow inside the DATAFLOW region
guards: NUM_TILES = (N + TILE_SIZE - 1) / TILE_SIZE must be compile-time friendly
last partial tile handled inside load/compute/store functions with guards

skills.pattern: #pragma HLS DATAFLOW wrapping a for (t = 0; t < TSTEPS; t++) loop that calls alternating compute tasks which read/write the same local arrays (stencil time steps, iterative relaxation)
skills.strategy: Temporal iteration (tsteps, time loops) belongs inside a single compute task, not as multiple concurrent DATAFLOW tasks in an outer t-loop. Use ping-pong locals (A_in/A_out or buf0/buf1) inside that one compute task for alternating read/write phases.
required_steps: detect outer t-loop or phase-loop inside #pragma HLS DATAFLOW
move the entire t-loop into one static compute_* task with INLINE off
use separate local arrays for alternating phases (local_A, local_B, local_A_new) — each array has one writer per iteration inside the compute task
keep DATAFLOW as load_task → compute_all_timesteps_task → store_task only
never call compute_phase_A and compute_phase_B as sibling tasks under DATAFLOW inside a shared t-loop
guards: fixes HLS 200-979 'can only be written in one process' on stencil locals
DATAFLOW overlap is load || compute || store, not per-timestep task parallelism
label inner t-loop and phase loops for audit

skills.pattern: #pragma HLS DATAFLOW wrapping multiple tasks that communicate only through shared local arrays or caller globals (no hls::stream, no ping-pong with proven overlap) while all m_axi ports use one bundle=gmem
skills.strategy: In the DATAFLOW refactor step, always keep `#pragma HLS DATAFLOW`. Prove producer–consumer overlap with hls::stream FIFOs, distinct gmemN bundles per port, or ping-pong buffers — fix structure until overlap is real. Never omit DATAFLOW or revert to sequential load → compute → store without the pragma.
required_steps: inspect every DATAFLOW region: list tasks, how data moves between them, and whether hls::stream or distinct bundles exist
reject task graphs where multiple concurrent tasks write the same local array without ping-pong or streams
reject parallel per-port loaders on shared bundle=gmem — rebundle to gmem0/gmem1/... first
require an overlap report (stage pairing | overlap? | evidence) and fix gaps with gmemN, streams, or ping-pong
never remove #pragma HLS DATAFLOW in this step — repair task boundaries instead
if ap_ctrl_none is used with DATAFLOW, prefer ap_ctrl_chain or fix task interfaces to avoid deadlock (HLS 200-656)
guards: increasing FIFO depth (HLS 200-1019/1020) is not a substitute for real overlap
tasks must not read caller m_axi arrays directly while also having a DATAFLOW predecessor (HLS 200-1449)
decorative multi-task DATAFLOW often loses to flash-selected sequential pipelined code

skills.pattern: ping-pong or double buffers (buf[2], tile&1, in_buf/out_buf alternation) across sequential tile iterations without load of tile t+1 overlapping compute or store of tile t
skills.strategy: Ping-pong is valid only when load of tile t+1 overlaps compute/store of tile t, or a clearly defined multi-stage dataflow pipeline overlaps independent tiles. If tiles run strictly sequentially with no concurrent stages, use a single local buffer.
required_steps: identify ping-pong buffer indexing (tile % 2, buf[0]/buf[1], in_ping/in_pong)
verify concurrent producer-consumer schedule: while computing tile t, loading tile t+1 (or storing t-1)
if stages still run serially per tile, remove ping-pong and use one local_A/local_b buffer
prioritize inner-loop II=1, memory copy placement, and reduction fixes before re-adding overlap
state in the response whether ping-pong provides actual overlap; remove if it does not
guards: doubling local BRAM without overlap increases resource pressure with no throughput gain
alternating buffer indices alone does not create hardware overlap

skills.pattern: for (tile = 0; tile < NUM_TILES; tile++) loop placed inside #pragma HLS DATAFLOW calling load tasks that read the same m_axi port each iteration — HLS instantiates parallel readers on one bundle (HLS 200-1013 / 200-984)
skills.strategy: Never put a tile-indexed for-loop inside #pragma HLS DATAFLOW if the loop body calls tasks that read/write m_axi ports. Either: (1) fuse all tile loads into one task with pipelined inner loops, (2) move the tile loop outside DATAFLOW into a helper that calls a per-tile DATAFLOW body with private buffers, or (3) use hls::stream tile pipeline (load_tile→compute_tile→store_tile) with depth≥2.
required_steps: detect for (i0 = 0; i0 < N; i0 += TILE_SIZE) inside #pragma HLS DATAFLOW
if body calls load_* tasks touching m_axi, refactor to single fused load OR stream pipeline
each m_axi port: at most one concurrent reader and one concurrent writer across DATAFLOW tasks
for multi-phase kernels (two passes over same matrix), preload full matrix into locals in one task before phased compute
verify csynth no longer reports bundled bus interface read in multiple processes
guards: distinct gmemN per port does not fix multiple concurrent readers on the same port
pair with hls-single-load-dual-local-layout when one matrix needs two access patterns
ARRAY_PARTITION local tile buffers for compute parallelism after fused load

skills.pattern: compute loops perform read-modify-write updates directly on arrays mapped to m_axi ports (e.g. A[i][j] = A[i][j] + expr, x[i] = x[i] + expr, w[i] = w[i] + expr inside nested loops)
skills.strategy: Treat every m_axi argument as external DRAM/HBM. Never read and write the same external element inside an inner loop. Do not use global/m_axi arrays as temporary storage or assume HLS will cache m_axi data across iterations.
required_steps: scan every loop for statements that read and write the same m_axi port element
reject direct accumulation into m_axi arrays
reject repeated reads of the same output element from DRAM/HBM inside an inner loop
reject repeated writes to the same output element inside an inner loop
replace with load-compute-store using local buffers or private scalar accumulators
for reductions, accumulate in a private scalar or local array, then write back once
if the full array is too large, tile/block but still finalize each tile locally before one store
guards: preserve numerical semantics when staging into locals
const read-only m_axi inputs may be read once per tile into locals
in-place outputs still require local write-back buffers, not inner-loop RMW on the port

skills.pattern: DATAFLOW region containing complex if/else, non-unit loop increments, or dynamic control logic instead of declarations and function calls
skills.strategy: Use canonical DATAFLOW regions: stream/buffer declarations and calls to load/compute/store subfunctions only. Move control logic, boundary handling, and non-unit loops outside or into subfunctions called from the dataflow region.
required_steps: split load, compute, store into separate functions
inside #pragma HLS DATAFLOW: declare hls::stream or ping-pong buffers and call subfunctions
move if/else tile guards into subfunctions or use bounded canonical loops
no non-unit stride loops or dynamic allocation inside the dataflow region
guards: subfunctions must be synthesizable with stable interfaces
fifo depths must cover producer-consumer latency

skills.pattern: triangular factorization, triangular solve, or other pivot-dependent tiled algorithms using ping-pong or DATAFLOW tile overlap without proving cross-tile dependence safety
skills.strategy: Algorithms with cross-tile dependencies (especially triangular factorization or solve with pivot-dependent active regions) require a dependence proof before overlapping tiles. Default to sequential tiles with local staging; do not assume ping-pong is legal.
required_steps: identify cross-tile read-after-write or triangular dependencies (pivot row, active column, forward substitution)
reject ping-pong/DATAFLOW across tiles unless dependence analysis shows independence
process dependent tiles sequentially; overlap only separate load/compute/store stages within one tile via canonical DATAFLOW if legal
document dependence reasoning when proposing any tile overlap
guards: numerical correctness overrides throughput — wrong overlap breaks triangular factorization/solve
pivot-dependent active regions make arbitrary tile overlap unsafe
do not include source benchmark names in agent-visible prompts
do not encode baseline-to-target sequences in skill IDs
do not expose private evaluator metadata
skills.pattern: agent attempts to infer or mention the source benchmark suite, hidden test design, target variant sequence, or expected optimization step from skill names or evaluation feedback
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: optimize only from current code, reports, constraints, and feedback; do not assume a benchmark family, stepwise target, or one-shot target

guards: do not duplicate large 2D/3D tiles blindly
check local memory resource budget
prefer smaller tile size or stream buffering when possible
skills.pattern: double buffering would duplicate large local arrays and exceed or severely pressure BRAM/URAM resources
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: reduce tile size, buffer only the required stream, use smaller staging buffers, or avoid double buffering if memory duplication outweighs overlap benefit

guards: ping-pong buffers alone do not guarantee overlap
check DATAFLOW report or schedule evidence
avoid adding memory overhead without reducing interval
skills.pattern: a proposed double-buffering transformation duplicates buffers but load, compute, and store phases still execute serially or cannot overlap because of dependencies
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: do not treat double buffering as complete unless stages actually overlap and interval/latency improves

guards: writing an intermediate to global memory only to read it in the immediately following phase is always suspect
this applies even when the intermediate is also an output port
skills.pattern: phase N writes an intermediate array to a global or m_axi output that phase N+1 immediately reads again, even though the value could remain in a local buffer
required_steps: detect producer phase writing global and consumer phase reading the same array
route to hls-chain-intermediate-results-locally
keep the intermediate in local memory until no later phase needs it
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: do not write intermediates to global memory between dependent phases; route to hls-chain-intermediate-results-locally

guards: avoid-tier skills must not cause fallback to unoptimized reference code
when in doubt, apply hls-baseline-load-compute-store-gate rather than emitting textbook C
skills.pattern: the model avoids advanced transforms because of many avoid rules or uncertainty, and responds with textbook nested loops on global arrays and no compute pragmas
required_steps: detect reference-port output despite loaded skill catalog
do not treat caution as permission to skip optimization
apply hls-baseline-load-compute-store-gate, hls-multi-phase-local-pipeline, or hls-iterative-stencil-timestep-local-volume as appropriate
ensure PIPELINE pragmas exist before submitting
skills.strategy: avoid rules forbid unsafe transforms, not all transforms; when uncertain, still apply the baseline local load-compute-store recipe instead of reference C
